targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing digital-employee runtimes and externally visible task state
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands schedulers, workers and lifecycle states.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A system can publish Running when it knows only that work was scheduled or claimed, causing downstream clients to act on a state stronger than the evidence.

whyNow: Anthropic's same-day available Claude Code v2.1.247 release note documents an affected self-hosted runner path that could report running before the Claude Code process started and trigger a premature desktop notification.

externalHook.description: A user-facing Running label escaped the control plane before the execution process existed.

coreProposition: An externally visible Running state should be published only after the runtime holds evidence sufficient for the execution-readiness semantics its consumers rely on; scheduling, assignment and worker claim must remain distinguishable from readiness, and the demonstrated process-start boundary does not prove full health.

originalValue.description: Treats each externally visible lifecycle state as an evidence claim whose threshold is derived from the promise downstream consumers rely on.

readerTakeaway: Separate Scheduled, Claimed, Starting and Running; define the minimum evidence for each consumer-visible state and keep stronger health claims outside a process-start observation.

supported: Anthropic published the v2.1.247 release note and reported the affected premature Running behavior.
The disclosed fix prevents the affected Running publication from preceding Claude Code process startup.
A downstream desktop client acted on the premature state.
unsupported: Full initialization or health after process start
uncertain: Whether the new gate is process spawn, handshake, heartbeat or another signal
How startup failure and timeout are represented

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general runtime-state truth principle without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The official release note supports a concrete false-state incident and a bounded ordering conclusion with clear operational implications.
